plan.title: Asked for a video link: a YouTube search phrase, no link, nothing invented

transcript.text:
Hey, I'm ZOH! I'll help you get better at one thing with a small step each day. Text "stop" anytime, and you can change how I coach whenever you want, just say "chill out" or "push me harder."

What's your name, and what are you looking to work on?

• Put AI to work for you
• Read & learn more (books, ideas, any topic)
• Start something on the side
• Focus & get more done
• Speak & connect better
• Get fitter
• Eat better
• Sleep better
• Learn a fun skill (Rubik's cube, card trick, play a song, drawing)
• Not sure? Let's figure it out together
Let's go, Dana! What kind of movement do you enjoy, or have you done before, like gym, walking, running, or home workouts?
I want to learn proper squats and deadlifts, never lifted before
Love that, Dana. Squats and deadlifts are a great place to start, and we'll build the form from zero. Where will you practice: a gym you already have, or at home?
is there a good video on squat form? send me a link

Good call to learn form first. I can't send links, but search YouTube for "barbell squat form for beginners" and "Starting Strength squat" (Mark Rippetoe is well known for teaching it). Watch one, not five.

Where will you practice: a gym you already have, or at home?

checks.reason: First text is exempt; it carries the intro, stop line, coaching-style line and name and goal question.
No markdown, hashtags or filler; the goal list is plain bullets.
Warm and energetic without being overfamiliar; no emoji row.
Asks for name and goal with the goal list, as onboarding requires.
States only what it does and the coaching controls it offers.
No wake or sleep or pushiness questions.
2 questions, allowed here (counted in code)
Two sentences, one question.
Plain text with no markdown or filler.
Enthusiastic opener 'Let's go, Dana!' without overfamiliarity.
Asks about movement history, which fits a fitness goal.
Dana had already named squats and deadlifts; asking about prior movement is a new question, though it lightly overlaps.
Invents nothing about Dana.
No prohibited question types.
one question (counted in code)
Two sentences with one question.
Plain text.
Warm and sincere; 'we'll build the form from zero' is encouraging without overfamiliarity.
Asks where Dana will practice, a relevant onboarding input.
Uses only what Dana said: squats, deadlifts, never lifted.
Asks about a place not yet given.
No prohibited question types.
one question (counted in code)
Four sentences including the question, above the three-sentence limit, though the link answer is one sentence.
Plain text; quoted search phrases are not markdown.
Direct and warm; 'Watch one, not five' is brisk but not harsh.
Ends on the practice-location question, which fits onboarding and is an unanswered question.
Repeats the location question only because Dana never answered it, which is allowed.
No link or video title invented; the claim that Rippetoe is well known for teaching squats is unverified and not from a lookup.
The off-topic video request gets a short, useful answer, then it returns to onboarding.
No prohibited question types.
one question (counted in code)

conversation.reason: Says it's ZOH, what it does, that stop works anytime, how to change coaching, and asks name and goal with the list.
Dana's name and goal were asked once and not repeated; the location question was repeated only after no answer.
Transcript ends before location, plan inputs or wrap-up, so the onboarding inputs were not covered.
No mismatch between goal and time or resources came up.
'Get fitter' is taken from the list and the follow-up stays on it.
The first text tells Dana she can change how ZOH coaches anytime.
Onboarding never reached the plan questions or a wrap-up before the transcript ends.
Four ZOH texts, well within the limit.
ZOH sends no link and names no video title; it gives YouTube search phrases, which the rule allows, but it doesn't look anything up and adds an unverified attribution.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the video request well: it sent no link or video title and gave only search phrases, then returned to asking where Dana will practise. It ran a little long in the last text, and the transcript ends before onboarding covered the inputs or wrapped up.
